researcher: claude, WebFetch of the vendor reference pages named in each fact (phase 88)

facts.claim: The service endpoint is https://tasks.googleapis.com and every method path starts with /tasks/v1.
facts.evidence: Reference page: 'Service endpoint https://tasks.googleapis.com'; tasks.list page request line GET https://tasks.googleapis.com/tasks/v1/lists/{tasklist}/tasks.

facts.claim: Task lists are read at GET /tasks/v1/users/@me/lists; tasks at GET /tasks/v1/lists/{tasklist}/tasks; a task is added with POST .../tasks, changed with PATCH or PUT .../tasks/{task}, removed with DELETE .../tasks/{task}.
facts.evidence: Reference page method tables: tasklists.list GET /tasks/v1/users/@me/lists; tasks.list GET, tasks.insert POST, tasks.patch PATCH, tasks.update PUT, tasks.delete DELETE under /tasks/v1/lists/{tasklist}/tasks.

facts.claim: POST /tasks/v1/lists/{tasklist}/clear exists (tasks.clear), and DELETE /tasks/v1/users/@me/lists/{tasklist} removes a whole list.
facts.evidence: Reference page tables: tasks.clear POST /tasks/v1/lists/{tasklist}/clear; tasklists.delete DELETE /tasks/v1/users/@me/lists/{tasklist}. What clear removes (completed tasks) is from memory, not the fetched page.

facts.claim: Listing tasks accepts the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/tasks or https://www.googleapis.com/auth/tasks.readonly.
facts.evidence: tasks.list page: 'Requires one of the following: .../auth/tasks, .../auth/tasks.readonly'. The top reference page did not list scopes.

facts.claim: A Google OAuth access token is sent as an Authorization: Bearer header.
facts.evidence: Neither fetched page states the header; this is Google's general OAuth 2.0 practice, from memory.

facts.claim: Only tasks.googleapis.com is called by the connection (obtaining the token happens outside it).
facts.evidence: Reference page service endpoint is the only host named.

facts.claim: Google has no hosted MCP server for Tasks.
facts.evidence: Not re-fetched for this sheet: the catalog 3 changelog records that Google's page lists no Tasks server; check the page before relying on it.

facts.claim: A Google OAuth access token is short-lived (about an hour) and needs renewing.
facts.evidence: From memory; the page was not fetched.

choices.decision: reads are the default read tier; add and complete use the default write tier; DELETE and clear ask first
choices.because: a deleted task or list and a cleared list cannot be taken back; adding or completing a task can

choices.decision: http-rest with a stored access token, not an OAuth-managed connection
choices.because: the http archetype supports bearer, basic and header keys only; there is no hosted Tasks MCP server to use the OAuth archetype

open: The access token does not refresh itself: a long-lived setup needs the OAuth refresh flow, which the http archetype does not offer.
The bearer header, the token lifetime and the absence of a hosted MCP server are unverified (f5, f7, f8).
Not run against the live service: no Google account was used.
